steps.name: Normalize and rank by fold change
caveats: Low-count genes produce extreme log2FC values that are pure sampling noise; the expression filter and the MA plot must make this visible.
Gene symbols may contain duplicates or empty strings — collapse or drop them explicitly and report how many rows were affected.
A large library-size difference between the two samples can masquerade as a global expression shift if normalization is skipped.
steps.context: Design is 1 treated vs 1 control, human liver bulk RNA-seq, raw integer salmon counts at gene-symbol level. No biological replication exists, so this step is the honest core of the analysis: an effect-size ranking, not a test.
steps.question: Which genes show the largest normalized expression change between the single treated liver sample and the single control liver sample in counts.csv?
constraints: Use the exact input paths given; do not assume any other file exists.
Do not compute or report p-values or FDR in this step — log2 fold change and expression level only.
Report the observed library sizes and normalization factors for both samples in the summary.
Apply and report a low-expression filter before ranking; state the number of genes retained out of 12,000.
Use the actual condition labels found in metadata.csv (treated/control as recorded) in all outputs and figure legends.
steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-no-replicates-1v1-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 3 columns: gene symbol + 2 sample columns) and /eval-full-32-without-no-replicates-1v1-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (2 rows, sample + condition) and confirm the sample column names in the counts matrix match the metadata sample IDs exactly, reporting any mismatch rather than reordering silently. Normalize for library size (edgeR TMM-scaled CPM and, alongside it, DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors) and report the two library sizes and the size-factor ratio, since a large depth imbalance is the main technical driver of apparent 1v1 differences. Filter to genes with adequate signal (e.g. CPM >= 1 in at least one sample AND a raw count >= 10 in at least one sample) and report how many of the 12,000 genes survive. Compute per-gene log2 fold change treated-vs-control on normalized counts with a pseudocount, and export a full ranked table (gene symbol, raw counts both samples, normalized counts both samples, log2FC, mean normalized expression). Produce an MA plot and a scatter of log2 normalized counts (treated vs control) with the identity line, plus the Spearman/Pearson correlation between the two samples as a global similarity measure. State explicitly in the output summary that with one sample per condition the log2FC is a point estimate with no variance estimate and no confidence interval.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked gene table with log2FC and normalized expression for all retained genes is written to disk.
Library sizes, size factors, number of genes passing the expression filter, and the treated-vs-control correlation are reported.
MA plot and treated-vs-control scatter figures are produced.
The summary states that no statistical inference is possible from n=1 per group.

steps.name: edgeR fixed-BCV descriptive ranking
caveats: It is easy to present the fixed-BCV FDR as if it were a real test result; the whole point of this step is to prevent that.
If the two BCV settings give very different significant-gene counts (expected), that divergence is the finding, not a problem to be smoothed over.
Genes with high counts in one sample only will dominate both rankings — check them against the raw counts for single-sample artifacts.
steps.context: With zero residual degrees of freedom, edgeR/DESeq2 cannot estimate dispersion. Supplying a fixed BCV is the standard, explicitly-documented workaround and it produces a defensible ranking, but the resulting p-values are a function of the analyst's assumption, not of the data. Showing the BCV=0.2 vs BCV=0.4 divergence is what makes that dependence concrete instead of a caveat sentence.
steps.question: Under externally assumed dispersion values, how are genes ordered between the treated and control liver sample, and how sensitive is that ordering to the assumed BCV?
constraints: Do NOT attempt estimateDisp, estimateGLMCommonDisp, or DESeq2's default dispersion estimation on this design — they have no residual degrees of freedom here.
Run both BCV = 0.4 and BCV = 0.2 and report both gene counts at FDR 0.05 and the rank correlation between them.
Every p-value/FDR column in exported tables must be named or documented so that its dependence on an assumed dispersion is unmissable.
The headline candidate gene list must be defined by effect size and expression level, not by the assumed-dispersion FDR.
steps.description: Using the filtered, normalized count matrix from T1S1, run edgeR's documented no-replicate workaround: estimateGLMCommonDisp is impossible, so fit exactTest with a fixed biological coefficient of variation supplied by the analyst — dispersion = 0.4^2 (BCV 0.4, the edgeR-recommended value for human tissue between subjects) as the primary run, and dispersion = 0.2^2 (BCV 0.2, genetically homogeneous / technical-replicate-like) as a sensitivity run. Export both ranked tables with logFC, logCPM, the nominal p-value and BH-adjusted value, but label every such column unambiguously as 'assumed-dispersion, not an inferential p-value' in the column names or an accompanying README. Quantify the sensitivity directly: number of genes below FDR 0.05 under each BCV, the Spearman rank correlation between the two gene rankings, and the overlap of the top 100 genes. Produce a volcano plot for the BCV=0.4 run with a clear caption stating the dispersion was assumed rather than estimated. Define a final descriptive candidate set as genes that are both in the top ranks by |log2FC| from T1S1 (e.g. |log2FC| >= 1) and above the expression floor, and report it as the primary gene list.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked tables for BCV=0.4 and BCV=0.2 are exported with explicitly labelled assumed-dispersion statistics.
Gene counts at FDR<0.05 under each BCV, the between-BCV Spearman rank correlation, and top-100 overlap are reported.
A volcano plot with an assumption-disclosing caption is produced.
A final descriptive candidate gene list defined by |log2FC| and expression floor is written to disk.

steps.name: Pathway-level shift on ranked list
caveats: Gene symbol mismatches between the counts matrix and the pathway GMT will silently shrink the tested universe — report the mapping rate.
The WikiPathways GMT descriptor field is '%'-delimited; split it to recover readable pathway names.
With one sample per condition, a strong NES can be driven by a handful of highly-expressed liver genes; inspect leading-edge membership before interpreting.
steps.context: Single-sample fold changes are noisy per gene but aggregate signal across a pathway can still be informative direction-wise. Tissue is liver, so xenobiotic and metabolic pathway sets are the ones most likely to carry a real treatment signal.
steps.question: Do the fold-change-ranked genes from the treated-vs-control liver comparison show any coordinated pathway-level shift that is more robust than individual gene calls?
constraints: Use human (Homo sapiens) gene sets only — the data is human liver; a mouse or rat collection would produce confident nonsense.
Rank the full filtered gene list by log2FC from T1S1; do not pre-threshold before the GSEA-style prerank run.
Report leading-edge genes for every pathway that is highlighted.
State in the output that enrichment p-values inherit the unreplicated single-pair ranking and are hypothesis-generating only.
steps.description: Take the full log2FC-ranked gene list from T1S1 (gene symbols, HGNC space) and run a rank-based gene set enrichment (fgsea or gseapy prerank) against human pathway gene sets. The reference the step needs is a human pathway gene-set collection keyed by HGNC gene symbols; resolve it against whatever the environment provides — the WikiPathways human collection is present in the reference store and is the expected match. Also run a simple overrepresentation test on the up- and down-regulated candidate sets from T1S2 as a cross-check. Report normalized enrichment scores, nominal and BH-adjusted values, and leading-edge genes for the top pathways in each direction, and restrict interpretation to liver-relevant biology (xenobiotic/CYP metabolism, lipid metabolism, acute-phase/inflammatory response, bile acid handling) where such sets appear. Because the underlying ranking comes from a single pair of samples, frame every result as hypothesis-generating: a coordinated multi-gene shift is more credible than any single gene, but it is still unreplicated and cannot be assigned a genuine false-discovery rate. If no human pathway gene-set resource is available at run time, report that the enrichment could not be run and deliver the ranked gene list alone — the primary DE deliverable does not depend on this step.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked enrichment table with NES, p-value, adjusted p-value and leading-edge genes is exported, or an explicit statement that no suitable human pathway resource was available.
The gene-symbol mapping rate between the counts matrix and the gene-set collection is reported.
Top enriched pathways are reported separately for the up and down directions with liver-relevant sets called out.
All enrichment results are explicitly labelled hypothesis-generating given the unreplicated design.

plan.title: 1v1 liver treated vs control: descriptive DE screen
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 2-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix from human liver (counts.csv, salmon gene-level integer counts keyed by gene symbol) with a 2-row metadata table giving one treated and one control sample. With n=1 per condition there is zero residual degrees of freedom, so no method can estimate within-condition biological variance from these data. Any p-value or FDR produced here is not a valid inferential statement about treatment effect — it can only reflect an assumed dispersion. The plan is therefore built to be honest about that rather than to manufacture significance.

T1S1 does library-size normalization (CPM/median-of-ratios) and computes per-gene log2 fold change between the treated and control sample, ranking genes by effect size with an expression floor to suppress the low-count noise that dominates 1v1 ratios. T1S2 runs edgeR exactTest with a fixed, externally assumed BCV (the documented no-replicate workaround: bcv=0.4 for human tissue, plus a bcv=0.2 sensitivity run) purely to order genes and to show how completely the gene ranking depends on the assumed dispersion; its outputs are labelled descriptive, not inferential. T1S3 is a ranked-list overrepresentation/GSEA-style pass on WikiPathways human sets (present in the reference store) using the fold-change ranking, because a coordinated pathway shift across many genes is more robust to single-sample noise than any individual gene call, and it is reported as hypothesis-generating only.

The deliverable is a prioritized, effect-size-ranked candidate gene list with an explicit statement that the design cannot support statistical inference and that follow-up requires biological replicates.
